findings.rule: REVIEW.md Framework rules: 'Flag when the change has made CLAUDE.md outdated' and 'The second occurrence of the same finding across reviews produces a one-line entry in CLAUDE.md ... proposed in the review for the owner'
findings.summary: CLAUDE.md's Layout entries for sample_pkg/calc.py (line 22) and sample_pkg/__init__.py (line 23) still list only add, divide and percent, so the guardrail file is now outdated about the package's public API now that mean ships; this is the same 'CLAUDE.md outdated' pattern already flagged in change 0001's review for percent, so this is a second occurrence and should produce a proposed one-line 'Things Claude gets wrong' entry for the owner (e.g. 'New public functions in sample_pkg/calc.py routinely leave CLAUDE.md's Layout section outdated until the owner applies the review's proposed line by hand').

mean's Collection[float] hint does not stop a str or dict from being passed (both are Collections): a str raises a TypeError from sum() and a dict silently averages its keys only, ignoring values, which could surprise a caller since neither is flagged in the docstring; not sure this is worth more than a doc note given it is an explicitly decided, reviewed contract.
